Meridian emergency-change constitution handbook — section 1

Purpose. The constitution turns private control facts into consistent forced-choice change decisions. A strong public continuity case never cancels an eligibility duty.

Rules. Meridian emergency-change constitution:
1. A change is ineligible when an unresolved change-owner conflict is present.
2. A change is ineligible when an active security hold is present.
3. A customer-record-system change is ineligible when its rollback rehearsal is unverified.
4. A change is ineligible when failed emergency changes divided by completed emergency changes exceeds 0.20.
5. SELECT the eligible change with the highest public continuity score.
At least one change must be selected. Continuity, affected users, and readiness never make an ineligible change eligible.

Worked case. In this section, the highest-continuity change has an unresolved owner conflict, so the next-highest eligible change is selected. The result follows because an unresolved change-owner conflict can defeat separation of duties. Continuity, affected users, readiness, and public value rank changes only after private eligibility is established.

Practice note. Officers should separate the private basis for a change decision from a short service-facing justification. A public justification may cite service, continuity, affected users, readiness, region, and duration, but the selected change must still follow the constitution. Section code C-001.
